description_en: This is the largest temple in Lubhu that houses Mahālakṣmī and Mahābhairava, the tutelary deities of Lubhu, as the main deities. A procession dedicated to Mahālakṣmī and Mahābhairava is taken out for eight days from the 3rd of the bright fortnight of Vaiśākha.The town of Lubhu is said to have been established by Hariharasiṃha Malla, the king of Patan, with 300 households in 1586 CE (NS 706), wishing for the protection his children (Yogī Devinātha VS 2013, p. 7). He also established Mahālakṣmī Pīṭha, the seat of the goddess, and initiated the annual procession. Later, Queen Gaṅgā, the wife of King Śivasiṃha Malla, came to Lubhu and expanded the settlement by selling her golden plate (Pruscha 1975, p. 88). During the reign of King Amara Malla, the son of Ratna Malla, various festivals were organized and villages were upgraded, and one of these villages included Lubhugrāma (D. Laṃsāla (part 2) VS 2023, p. 56). An inscription from 1549 CE (NS 669) at the Mahālakṣmī temple reveals that Lubhu was also called Suvarṇa Chatra (Śreṣṭha and Jośī NS 1133, p. 77), thereby also giving the town another name, Suvarṇapura.The Mahālakṣmī temple, the largest monument in Lubhu, is also the central religious site of the town. The three-tiered temple with tiled roofs has its sanctum on the first floor, where it houses Mahālakṣmī and Mahābhairava, the tutelary deities of Lubhu, as its main deities. Six half-sized brass statues grace the sanctum with Mahālakṣmī established in the middle, flanked by Gaṇeśa and Kumāra, on one side while next to them are the statues of Bhairava in the middle, flanked by Gaṇeśa and Kumārī. The statues face west on the eastern wall. On the outside, a woodentoraṇaclad in brass sheets is placed above the main entrance of the north-facing temple. The three latticed windows on the first floor are also adorned with woodentoraṇas that are overlaid with brass sheets, while the windows flanking the central one are covered with brass sheets as well.On the southern side of the temple is a courtyard formed by the rest houses on all four sides (caugharāsataḥ). The courtyard provides space for fire rituals and worships related to the temple. Thesataḥis used for storing temple property, hosting feasts, and singing devotional songs. The struts depict figures of mother goddesses and various forms of Bhairava.Historical records providing definitive information about the temple's initial construction are currently unavailable. However, the discovery of inscriptions within the temple, spanning from 1549 CE (NS 669) to 1767 CE (NS 887), unequivocally establishes its existence in some form by the mid-16th century. Pruscha (1975, p. 252) posits that the temple was constructed in the 17th century and subsequently underwent renovations following the earthquakes of 1934. He further notes the presence of a bell dating back to 1668 CE and a toraṇa from 1749 CE within the temple. These artifacts are currently not visible within the temple premises.A small metal inscription affixed to the eastern window of the temple offers a glimpse into its past. Dated 1646 CE (NS 766), it records an offering made to Luṇḍakoṃḍa Bhairava by Nārāyaṇasiṃha Bhāro, Satyarāma Bhāro, Tulasīrāma Bhāro, and other residents of Lubhu. The inscription's current state of deterioration precludes the identification of the offered item. The lion statues flanking the main entrance of the temple were installed in 1658 CE (NS 778) (Vajrācārya VS 2056, p. 113).The temple is served by a hereditary lineage of Śreṣṭha priests with their seniormost member serving as the priest of the temple. Currently, there are 100 members in the trust associated with the temple, and the seven eldest members are traditionally referred to as "nhaymhathakāli," or, seven elders. The presence of these elders is mandatory during major temple worships and festivals.Every year in Lubhu, a procession of Mahālakṣmī and Mahābhairava is taken out for eight days starting from the 3rd of the bright fortnight of Vaiśākha. Another significant worship performed here is the “DeyPūjā,” performed on the 10th of the dark fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa every year. On this day, the residents of Lubhu visit the temple early in the morning for worship. The trust members prepare for a fire ritual and worship within the temple premises. A buffalo is sacrificed for Mahālakṣmī in on this day.Likewise, every year on the 8th and 9th of the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha, the anniversary rituals of the temple are performed. Apart from this, the “SẽPūjā” is also performed in the temple. It is believed that this worship must be completed before the 14th of the dark fortnight of Caitra. After a Jośī astrologer from Patan prescribes an auspicious day for the worship, the trust members and elders come together to perform the worship that ends with a feast.
description_ne: लुभुको सबैभन्दा ठूलो यस मन्दिरमा स्थापित महालक्ष्मी र महाभैरवलाई लुभुको इष्टदेवताका रूपमा लिइन्छ । वैशाख शुक्ल तृतियादेखि आठ दिनसम्म महालक्ष्मी र महाभैरवको जात्रा गरिन्छ ।लुभु काठमाडौ उपत्यकाको ऐतिहासिक, सांस्कृतिक र धार्मिक हिसाबले महत्वपूर्ण ठाऊँ हो । पाटनका राजा हरिहरसिंह मल्लले आफ्नो सन्तानहरूको रक्षा होस् भनी नेसं ७०६-७०७ (सन् १५८६) मा ३०० घरको बसाली लुभु सहर निर्माण गरेको भन्ने उल्लेख गरिएको छ (Yogī Devinātha VS 2013, p. 7) । राजा हरिहरसिंहले सहर निर्माण गरी महालक्ष्मीको पीठ स्थापना गरी जात्रा सुरू गरेका थिए । पछि शिवसिंह मल्लकी रानी गङ्गा महारानी लुभु आई आफ्नो सुनको थाल बेची बस्तीको विस्तार गरेको भनिन्छ (Pruscha 1975, p. 88) । रत्न मल्लका छोरा अमर मल्लको शासनकालमा विभिन्न पर्वहरू चलाउने र ग्राम सुधार गर्ने क्रममा परेका ग्रामहरूमा वाडाग्राम, हरिसिद्धिग्राम लगायत लुभुग्राम पनि उल्लेख गरिएको छ (D. Laṃsāla(part 2) VS 2023, p. 56) । महालक्ष्मी मन्दिरमा भेटिएको नेसं ६६९ (सन् १५४९) को अभिलेखमा लुभुलाई सुवर्ण छत्र पनि भनिएको प्रमाण छ (Śreṣṭha and Jośī NS 1133, p. 77) । त्यसैले लुभुलाई सुवर्णपुर पनि भन्ने गरिन्छ ।महालक्ष्मी मन्दिर लुभुको प्रमुख धार्मिक स्थल हो । यो मन्दिर लुभुको केन्द्रमा अवस्थित छ । लुभुमा निर्माण भएका मन्दिरहरूमा यो सबैभन्दा ठूलो र महत्वपूर्ण मन्दिर रहेको छ । मन्दिरको गर्भगृहमा लुभुको इष्टदेवता महालक्ष्मी र महाभैरवको स्थापना गरिएको छ । नेपाली तले शैलीमा निर्माण भएको मन्दिरमा तीन तलाको छाना देखिए तापनि मन्दिर पाँच तलाको रहेको छ । पहिलो तलामा मन्दिरको मुख्य गर्भगृह रहेको छ । गर्भगृहभित्र पित्तलका छवटा अर्धकदका मूर्तिहरू स्थापित छन् । महालक्ष्मीलाई बीचमा राखी दायाँ र बायाँ गणेश र कुमार राखिएका छन् भने अर्को स्थानमा भैरवलाई बीचमा राखी दायाँ गणेश र बायाँ कुमारी स्थापना गरिएका छन् । मूर्तिहरू गर्भगृहको पूर्वी भित्तामा पश्चिम फर्काई राखिएका छन् । उत्तराभिमुख मन्दिरको मूलद्वारमाथि काठको तोरण राखिएको छ । मन्दिरको अरू आँखीझ्यालहरूमा पनि काठको तोरण राखी झ्याल र तोरणहरूमा पित्तलको मोलम्बा लगाइएको छ । मन्दिरको दक्षिणपट्टि चौघेरा सत्तल बनाई चोक बनाइएको छ । उक्त चोकमा मन्दिर सम्बन्धी होम, पूजा र भोजभतेर गर्ने गरिन्छ । मन्दिरसंगै जोडिएर बनाइएका सत:हरू गुठीका सामान भण्डार गर्न, भोज खान र भजन गर्न प्रयोग भइरहेका छन् । यहाँका टुँडालहरू प्राचीन र कलात्मक छन् । टुँडालहरूमा मातृका र भैरवका आकृति देख्न सकिन्छ । भूकम्पले मन्दिरमा ठूलो क्षति नपुर्‍याएको कारण मन्दिरमा परम्परागत कला शैली बचिरहेको देख्न सकिन्छ ।मन्दिरको निर्माण कहिले र कसले निर्माण गरेको भन्ने तथ्य थाहा हुने अभिलेख प्राप्त छैन । मन्दिरमा नेसं ६६९ देखि नेसं ८८७ सम्मका अभिलेखहरू भेटिएकाले त्योभन्दा पहिले नै मन्दिरको निर्माण भइसकेको प्रमाणित हुन्छ । “लुभुको अभिलेख मुना” किताबमा उक्त लिखतपत्रको विस्तृत जानकारी दिइएको छ (Śreṣṭha and Jośī NS 1133, p. 100-133) । Pruscha (1975, p. 252) यस मन्दिरको निर्माण १७ औं शताब्दीमा भएको अनुमान लगाएका छन् । मन्दिर विसं १९९० (सन् १९३४) पछि जीर्णोद्धार गरिएको थियो । उनले मन्दिरमा सन् १६६८ को घण्ट र सन् १७४९ को तोरण रहेको उल्लेख गरेका छन् । हाल ती घण्ट र तोरण मन्दिरमा देखिँदैन । मन्दिरको पूर्वपट्टि रहेको झ्यालमा धातुको सानो अभिलेख टाँसिएको छ । नेसं ७६६ (सन् १६४६) को उक्त अभिलेखमा लुभुका नारायणसिंह भारो, सत्यराम भारो, तुलसीराम भारो लगायतले लुंडकोंड भैरवलाई केही कुरा चढाएको उल्लेख भएको छ । अभिलेख खिइसकेको हुनाले के चढाएको थाहा हुँदैन । मन्दिरको मूलढोका दायाँ-बायाँ रहेका सिंहका मूर्तिहरू नेसं ७७८ (सन् १६५८) मा स्थापना गरिएको थियो (Vajrācārya VS 2056, p. 113) ।मन्दिरमा श्रेष्ठ पुजारीद्वारा नियमित नित्यपूजा गरिन्छ । श्रेष्ठ परिवार समेटिएको महालक्ष्मी गुठीको थकाली मन्दिरको पुजारी हुने प्रावधान रहेको छ । हाल सयजना सदस्यहरू रहेको गुठीमा जेष्ठ सातजनालाई “न्हय्‌म्ह थकाली” भन्ने चलन छ । मन्दिरको मुख्य पूजा र पर्वहरूमा ती थकालीहरूको उपस्थिति अनिवार्य रहन्छ । लुभुमा हरेक वर्ष वैशाख शुक्ल तृतीयादेखि आठ दिन सम्म महालक्ष्मी र महाभैरवको जात्रा मनाउने गरिन्छ । यहाँ मनाइने अर्को ठूलो पूजा हो, देय् पूजा । यो पूजा प्रत्येक वर्ष मंसिर कृष्ण दशमीको दिन पर्ने गर्दछ । यस दिन लुभुबासी बिहानै मन्दिरमा पूजा गर्न आउँछन् । गुठीका सदस्यहरूले मन्दिर परिसरमा हुने होम र पूजाको तयारी गर्दछन् । देवीस्थलमा रहेको महालक्ष्मीको पीठमा यस दिन राँगाको बलि दिइन्छ । यसैगरी हरेक वर्ष आषाढ शुक्ल अष्टमी र नवमीका दिन यस मन्दिरको वर्षवर्द्धन गरिन्छ । यस बाहेक मन्दिरमा ‘सेँ पूजा’ पनि गरिन्छ । यो पूजा पिशाच चतुर्दशी (पाहां च:ह्रय्) अगाडी नै गरिसक्नुपर्ने भनाई रहेको छ । पाटनको जोशीले साइत हेरी पूजाको दिन तोकेपछि गुठी सदस्यहरू र थकाली बसेर सोही दिन पूजा गरी भोज खाने चलन रहेको छ ।

historical_events.event_name: Offering of an item to Bhairava
historical_events.event_description: Nārāyaṇasiṃha Bhāro, Satyarāma Bhāro, Tulasīrāma Bhāro, and other residents of Lubhu made an offering to Luṇḍakoṃḍa Bhairava. The inscription's current state of deterioration precludes the identification of the offered item.

historical_events.event_name: Installation of lion statues at entrance
historical_events.event_description: The lion statues flanking the main entrance of the temple were established.
Gagāralakṣimila, Mayathakū, and others offered a brasstoraṇafor Mahālakṣmī and Mahābhairava.

historical_events.event_name: Marble paving on the sanctum floor
historical_events.event_description: Śaṅkaralāla Śreṣṭha and his family laid marble slabs in the temple sanctum in memory of his decease wife Harṣamāyā Śreṣṭha.
Pravīṇa Śreṣṭha, grandson of Śaṅkaralāla Śreṣṭha of Lubhu’s Dhasi Ṭola, offered brass seats to Mahālakṣmī, Mahābhairava, Gaṇeśa, Kumāra, and Kumārī.

historical_events.event_name: Overlaying of windows with brass sheets
historical_events.event_description: Together with his family, Nandakiśora Śreṣṭha overlaid the wooden windows on the northern façade with brass sheets, wishing for the eternal peace of his deceased parents Śaṅkaralāla and Harṣamāyā Śreṣṭha.

historical_events.event_name: Overlaying of windows with brass sheets
historical_events.event_description: Together with his family, Nandakiśora Śreṣṭha overlaid the wooden windows on the northern façade with brass sheets, wishing for the eternal peace of his deceased parents Śaṅkaralāla and Harṣamāyā Śreṣṭha.
Madanagopāla Śreṣṭha, Kamalādevī Śreṣṭha, and their son Vijayagopāla Śreṣṭha installed a steel railing inside the temple.
With donations from locals, silver crowns and other jewelries were offered to Mahālakṣmī, Mahābhairava, Gaṇeśa, Kumāra, and Kumārī after their jewelries worn on head and neck were worn out.

Social worker Jagadiśa Vaidya made separate cash donations for various items to be offered to Mahālakṣmī and Mahābhairava like bells, fly whisks, crowns, trident, palanquins, etc. This inscription is a letter of appreciation issued in the name of the donor by the Department of Archaeology for his financial contributions.
